newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU cut flour refund after rejecting export bids.
newsitem.headline: EU cut flour refund after rejecting export bids.

text.p: The European Commission took the rare step of cutting its flour refund between weekly grain meetings after rejecting export bids for 140,000 tonnes at a higher level to prevent speculation, an EU official said on Thursday.
French grain office ONIC said earlier the European Union had cut its standing daily export refund for soft wheat flour to 10 Ecus per tonne from 17 Ecus per tonne, effective Wednesday.
"To avoid speculation on flour we rejected the bids and reduced the refund for flour," an EU official said.
The bids for refunds of 17 Ecus were rejected during a three-day discretion period earlier this week, he said.

The Commission can alter the refunds in its daily export channel, known as common right, at any time. But changes are more usually timed to coincide with a parallel weekly grain export tender each Thursday.
The official said the Commission decided to move against the flour export bids after studying a sharp drop in underlying wheat refunds traded on the open market.

Dealers said wheat refunds, which serve as a guide for flour support, were changing hands as low as eight Ecus per tonne this week compared with the last official EU award of 12.90 Ecus per tonne, as exporters scrambled to cover short positions.
Traders can sell licences that entitle them to EU export subsidies, recovering the difference between the face value and the traded value from the buyer when the market is short.
Some traders have said the EU industry is short of licences to cover up to a million tonnes of previous business, though others dispute this, saying the market's exposure is not clear.
The European Commission is seen as reluctant to leave too wide a window between the value of wheat refunds and wheat flour export refunds to avoid a run on flour exports.
Flour refunds are traditionally set at or near a level 1.37 times the underlying restitutions for wheat grain.
